outline_action: Cite this study as the key evidence for human diet intervention affecting ICI efficacy in melanoma, highlighting the significant EFS benefit and safety profile. Explicitly note that while the trial design targeted microbiome modulation as the primary objective, the microbiome data linking diet to efficacy is not detailed in this abstract and requires reference to companion publications or full results to satisfy the mechanistic success criterion. Use the heterogeneity across cohorts (neoadjuvant/unresectable vs. adjuvant) to discuss context-dependency of dietary interventions.
remaining_gap: The success criterion requires reporting microbiome changes alongside ICI efficacy to establish a causal chain (diet -> microbiome -> efficacy). While this study is the specific interventional trial design needed, the supplied text does not report the primary outcome data regarding microbiome structure or function changes, nor does it present mediation analysis linking microbiome shifts to the observed clinical benefits (EFS, ORR). Therefore, based solely on this text, the mechanistic link 'via microbiome changes' remains unconfirmed, even though the interventional efficacy signal is present.
useful_material: This study conducted a proof-of-principle randomized controlled trial with fully controlled feeding in melanoma patients receiving immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). It compared a High Fiber Diet Intervention (HFDI, ramped to 50 g/d) against a healthy control diet (20 g/d). The authors reported exploratory cancer-specific outcomes showing that in the combined neoadjuvant/unresectable cohort (n=24), the HFDI arm had a median event-free survival (EFS) not reached versus 20 months in control (p=0.03), and an objective response rate (ORR) of 77% versus 29% (p=0.06). In the adjuvant cohort, recurrence rate was 14% (HFDI) versus 33% (control). Any grade immune-related adverse events (IRAEs) were lower in the HFDI arm (71.4% vs 93.3%). The study design explicitly states the primary objective was to establish effects on gut microbiome structure and function, confirming the trial was designed to test the diet-microbiome-efficacy axis.

这项研究（DIET 试验，NCT04645680）是一项在黑色素瘤患者中进行的二期随机双盲饮食干预试验，比较了高纤维饮食（30-50 克/天）与健康对照饮食（20 克/天）对免疫检查点阻断（ICB）疗效的影响。摘要报告了早期结果显示高纤维饮食干预可行且治疗结果有改善前景。研究通过外周血单核细胞（PBMC）分析发现，高纤维组在第 5-8 周循环单核细胞、树突状细胞减少，效应记忆 T 细胞增加，且 T 细胞激活信号通路增强。此外，研究进行了人至小鼠的粪便微生物移植（FMT）实验，接受高纤维饮食后患者粪便的小鼠表现出更好的 ICB 反应和类似的免疫细胞变化，提示这种益处具有微生物组依赖性。

This study describes a proposed prospective dietary intervention clinical trial design targeting melanoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The authors plan to implement a sequential intervention involving a high-fermented food diet followed by high-fiber supplementation. The study aims to longitudinally assess gut microbial signatures and evaluate distinct immunological, proteomic, and metabolomic effects associated with these dietary modifications.
